items.prompt: I work in a clinical genomics unit that sequences tumours for a regional cancer registry. Over five years we have accumulated whole-exome somatic calls for 268 endometrial cancers. Mutation counts per gene are in a samples-by-genes CSV. We also have a CSV of exon lengths per gene, the cancer-gene list distributed with SAMBAR, and the MSigDB canonical pathways GMT. Gene-level analyses have been frustrating because the matrix is extremely sparse and hypermutated tumours dominate everything. I read that converting mutations to pathway-level scores, normalised for gene length and mutation burden, makes subtyping much more stable. We would like pathway mutation scores for every tumour and a clustering of the tumours into between three and five subgroups. Our clinicians will later check whether the subgroups line up with the molecular classification, but that is not something we need from you. Outputs can go to /registry/sambar_run1.

requirements.words: pathway mutation scores for every tumour
requirements.note: All four SAMBAR inputs are stated; gene-length and burden normalisation are SAMBAR transformations (sambar.yaml; Kuijjer et al. 2018).

requirements.words: a clustering of the tumours into between three and five subgroups
requirements.note: cluster=true with kmin=3, kmax=5 is within sambar.yaml limits for 268 samples.

items.m2_target: no delivery line for the output folder; both SAMBAR results available

items.prompt: I'm a postdoc in a reproductive biology group and I'm new to network methods. Over the last two years we collected endometrial biopsies from 44 women at different points of the menstrual cycle. Our core processed the RNA-seq, and we have a gene-by-sample matrix of variance-stabilised counts. We already ran DESeq2 and found a few hundred genes that change between the proliferative and secretory phases. My PI suspects that a handful of transcription factors orchestrate these changes, but differential expression alone can't show that. A colleague pointed me to a human promoter motif prior, which I have downloaded, together with a TF-TF interaction file from STRING. What we would like first is a single regulatory network that summarises how TFs target genes across all 44 biopsies. We will look at phase-specific questions later ourselves. Please keep everything under results/endometrium/.

requirements.words: a single regulatory network that summarises how TFs target genes across all 44 biopsies
requirements.note: Expression, motif prior and TF PPI are all stated, which is the aggregate TF-gene contract of PANDA (panda.yaml) and also OTTER/GIRAFFE; the output folder is a harmless choice.
